tasks.short: Inspect security features for compliance with standards.

steps.what: Show the applicable standards and regulations
Inspect physical security design features and installations
Judge compliance of the programs with those standards

outputs: filed copy of signed inspection v1

tasks.design: A job shows the applicable standards and regulations stored in {DOCS}. The specialist inspects physical security design features, installations, and programs and judges compliance. They sign the inspection. A job files that version. A standard that is not stored is not cited.
tasks.previous_blocker: A checklist could say a feature complied when nobody had looked.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored standards can be shown on the inspection.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the installation complies is still seen on the site.
tasks.altitude: The inspection stays. Finding the stored standard shrinks.

evidence.claim: The operations digest says reports and records can be a dashboard on the existing records.
Digest [S27] records that a model-drafted report cited sources that did not exist, so every cited clause or record must match a stored row.

assumptions: Nothing is filed as compliant before signature.
unknowns: Which standards apply to this site.
research_questions: How often the stored standard is out of date.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining time on the inspection is the looking itself, already the person's work.

incremental.description: Update the stored standard list or the drawing index when it changes, and clear drafts the specialist rejects.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes every feature is still inspected by the specialist. The high end assumes only the stored standard is no longer hunted by hand. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Audit physical security and staff safety vulnerabilities.

steps.what: Conduct security audits of the physical site
Identify potential vulnerabilities for staff safety

outputs: filed copy of signed security audit v1

tasks.design: Conducting security audits, and identifying potential vulnerabilities in physical security or staff safety, stays with the specialist on the site. A job files the audit in {DOCS} only after they sign it. The audit is of the site, not a score of named staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: A staff list could be treated as the vulnerability.
tasks.enabler_now: A signed audit can be filed on the existing record.
tasks.still_hard: What is vulnerable is still seen on the site.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist conducts the audit and signs it.
tasks.altitude: The audit stays. Filing the signed audit shrinks.

reach.learn: That it is not a staff score

evidence.claim: Digest [S23] says works-council consent is required before staff monitoring, so this design does not add a view of named staff.
Digest [S17] treats worker evaluation as high-risk, and digest [S18] places those duties from 2 December 2027, so security records are not turned into a staff evaluation.
Digest [S22] says a data protection assessment is mandatory for employee monitoring, so an automated watch of named staff is not built.

unknowns: Which areas are in the audit.
research_questions: How often a vulnerability is already on an open action.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining time on the audit is the walk itself, already the person's work.

incremental.description: Update the stored standard list or the drawing index when it changes, and clear drafts the specialist rejects.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes the specialist still walks the audit. The high end assumes only the signed audit is no longer copied. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design policies for alarms, access cards, and other needs.

steps.what: Design security policies for alarm response
Draft practices from the stored standards

loop.purpose: Draft a policy sentence only from the specialist's outline and a stored standard.
loop.input: The outline and the stored standard clauses.
loop.output: A policy draft that cites a clause id.
loop.check: Every clause id in the draft is in the stored standard.
loop.stop: Stop when a sentence has no clause id, or when the outline does not cover that practice.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template cannot tell which alarm practice this site needs.

steps.what: Design programs for access card use and other needs

outputs: filed copy of signed security policy v1

tasks.design: The specialist designs security policies, programs, and practices for alarm response, access-card use, and other security needs. A bounded draft in {DOCS} may phrase a sentence only from their outline and a stored standard. They sign the policy. A job files that version. A sentence with no clause id is dropped. The job does not issue a card or change an alarm.
tasks.previous_blocker: A generated practice could cite a standard nobody had opened.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored standards can be quoted into a draft.
tasks.still_hard: What is adequate for this site is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist designs the policy and signs it.

ambition.what: Revise a policy when a stored standard changes, and sign it again.

tasks.altitude: The design stays. Hunting the clause id shrinks.

evidence.claim: The operations digest says a draft must work from approved sources, and a named person signs.
Digest [S27] records that a model-drafted report cited sources that did not exist, so every cited clause or record must match a stored row.

assumptions: The draft is not the policy.
The job does not change a live alarm.
unknowns: Who may approve an access practice.
research_questions: How often the stored standard lags the official text.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining time on the design is the policy judgement, already the person's work.

incremental.description: Update the stored standard list or the drawing index when it changes, and clear drafts the specialist rejects.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes every cited clause is still opened by the specialist. The high end assumes only a sentence with no clause id comes back. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Test security measures and set how they are monitored.

steps.what: Test security measures for final acceptance
Provide procedures for ongoing monitoring and evaluation
List past test dates for the measure, not for a person
Sign the acceptance and the procedure

outputs: filed copy of signed acceptance v1

tasks.design: The specialist tests the security measures for final acceptance and provides the procedures for ongoing monitoring and evaluation of those measures. A dashboard in {BI} lists past test dates of the measure and does not name a person. The specialist signs. A job files that version. The job does not turn a measure on or off.
tasks.previous_blocker: A date on a chart could be treated as acceptance.
tasks.enabler_now: Past signed tests can be listed.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the measure passes, and how it should be watched, is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist tests, accepts, and signs the procedure.

ambition.what: File the acceptance the same day as the test, and only the signed version.

tasks.altitude: The test stays. Listing past dates shrinks.

reach.learn: That a date is not acceptance

evidence.claim: The operations digest says reports and records can be a dashboard on the existing records.
Digest [S23] says works-council consent is required before staff monitoring, so this design does not add a view of named staff.
Digest [S22] says a data protection assessment is mandatory for employee monitoring, so an automated watch of named staff is not built.

assumptions: The list is of measures, not of staff.
Nothing goes live from this job.
unknowns: How often a measure must be retested.
research_questions: How often a past test was signed for a different version of the measure.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining time on the test is the test itself, already the person's work.

incremental.description: Update the stored standard list or the drawing index when it changes, and clear drafts the specialist rejects.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes every measure is still tested by the specialist. The high end assumes only past test dates are no longer copied. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

role.altitude: The security specialist spends the week on the site, the incident, and the decision. Filing a signed note can move. No model scores a person, watches staff, or changes a live security system.
reach: A client sees only the criteria or the finding the specialist signed.
A supervisor gets an emergency note after the specialist has already responded.
skills_to_grow: Tell a stored incident count from a threat decision.
Refuse a view that scores or tracks named staff.
role.ambitious_version: A signed test or a signed recommendation can be filed the same day, and the specialist still decides it.
